Dick Katz
Pianist Dick Katz was born in Baltimore, Maryland on March 13,1924.

He studied piano at the Manhattan School of Music and received on-the-job training with J.J. Johnson and Kai Winding. Dick has performed and recorded with a long list of jazz luminaries including Benny Carter, Sonny Rollins and Roy Eldridge. He co-founded Milestone Records with Orrin Keepnews in Dick was interviewed in New York City on January 7, 2002 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Manhattan. I’m very, very pleased to have Dick Katz with me today, pianist and arranger, and veteran of the New York scene. Is that a decent introduction?
Yeah that’s okay.
Okay. I think I was going to —
They’ve got me to write a lot recently too, not in the last few years.
To be a writer?
I’ve written a lot of stuff.
Great. Let me read something that was said about you in the New Grove Encyclopedia of Jazz.
It’s all wrong.
Well it says—
It’s my fault I never corrected it. They sent a form years ago, and I never sent it in.
Well this is just a description.
Okay.
He says, “He has an eclectic style which reflects to some degree Teddy Wilson but also draws inspiration from Thelonious Monk and Bill Evans.”
Okay. Among others. But that part in there about West Coast — what does it say?
Oh —
They’ve got it all wrong. I’ve never worked on the West Coast.
Okay.
So they lump me together with those guys.
We can correct that today.
Okay.
